clue.text: What's left in Parisian art gallery

parts.note: in French 'tu es' means 'thou art', so a Parisian's art is es
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: A puzzled visitor asks what remains on show in a Paris art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art' here is the old verb form, as in 'thou art', not painting; its French equivalent is ES.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's estate is the property they leave behind at death, so it is literally what remains to heirs.

clue.text: Dirty pictures finish on top

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for pictures is lifted up to the top of this down entry

parts.note: oils are paintings, i.e. pictures

explanation.surface: A prudish complaint that smutty pictures end up on top of the pile.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'on top' means at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To dirty something is to stain or besmirch it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Redecorate Gaelic bar with symbols for numbers

indicators.note: to redecorate is to rework a room, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to do up an Irish pub, adding numbered signs.
explanation.definitionFit: Algebra replaces numbers with letters and other symbols, so algebraic working uses symbols standing for numbers.

clue.text: Start to educate Catholic in the present moral code

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
Catholic sits inside the word for the present

parts.note: 'this' points to the present one, as in 'this week'

explanation.surface: A call to teach Catholic values in today's schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethics are the principles of right conduct, i.e. a system of morals.

clue.text: Woods manages to keep still

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it within, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: to cope is to manage
a still is a photograph, informally a pic

explanation.surface: A forester's note that the woods somehow stay quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Coppices are small managed woodlands cut back periodically to encourage new growth.

clue.text: 17 to surpass skill British possess

parts.note: to cap something is to outdo it
ability is skill
to own is to possess

explanation.surface: Someone striving to outdo the skill the British have.
explanation.walkthrough: Capability Brown was the great 18th-century English landscape gardener; his real first name is the answer at 17 across.
explanation.definitionFit: The landscape gardener was christened with the knightly first name and nicknamed for his talk of a site's 'capabilities'.

clue.text: Carpenter's job limits new council's responsibility

indicators.note: to limit something is to enclose it on both sides, so one word holds the other

parts.note: a carpenter smooths wood by planing it

explanation.surface: A carpenter's work is restricted by the local council's rules.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain local councils grant or refuse permission for building work, so this control is their duty.

clue.text: Hibernian girl hit it off

parts.note: Iris is a girl's name

indicators.note: 'it off' says the letters of 'it' are taken away from the word before

explanation.surface: An Irish girl got on well with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit it off' looks like the idiom for getting on; it is an instruction to remove IT from HIT, leaving H.
explanation.definitionFit: Hibernia is the Latin name for Ireland, so Hibernian is an adjective meaning of Ireland.

clue.text: Uprooted old Irishman, ready to drop trousers

parts.note: ex- means former, i.e. old

indicators.note: used as a verb: to trouser is to pocket, so the word for weary takes in the name

parts.note: someone ready to drop is tired
Pat is a stock name for an Irishman

explanation.surface: An exhausted old Irishman about to let his trousers fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' is a verb meaning pockets, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To extirpate is to root out completely, so uprooted is a synonym.

clue.text: Elvis's joint position of authority

parts.note: Elvis Presley was nicknamed the King, so Elvis's is king's
the hip is a joint

explanation.surface: Elvis Presley's hip, a famous swivelling joint, held a position of power.
explanation.definitionFit: The office of a monarch is the highest seat of power in a kingdom.

clue.text: Noble poplar is topped, with sides lopped

indicators.note: cutting off the outer letters on each side of this phrase leaves the letters inside

explanation.surface: A grand poplar tree has been pruned at the top and sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristo is informal for aristocrat, a member of the nobility.

clue.text: Most MPs' patrons tour mountain chain

indicators.note: to tour is to go around, so the patrons surround the other pieces

parts.note: backers are sponsors or patrons
ben is a Scottish word for a mountain
CH is an abbreviation for chain, an old unit of length

explanation.surface: Members of Parliament's sponsors visit a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: Backbenchers are MPs without ministerial or shadow posts, who make up the majority of the House of Commons.

clue.text: Admin guy meets spy handling Middle East

parts.note: a guy is a man

indicators.note: the spy has the region in hand, i.e. holds it within

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: An office man meets a spy who is running Middle East operations.
explanation.definitionFit: Admin, short for administration, and this word both mean the running of an organisation.

clue.text: Ditch dance, ejecting hundreds

indicators.note: throwing out removes those letters from the dance

parts.note: the cha-cha is a Latin dance
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so hundreds are two Cs

explanation.surface: An order to abandon the dance, throwing out hundreds of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ditch' looks like a verb meaning abandon; it is a noun, a sunken boundary fence.
explanation.definitionFit: A ha-ha is a sunken ditch or wall bounding a park, keeping livestock out without blocking the view.

clue.text: Bath site, area covered by extended rental

parts.note: long means extended

indicators.note: the area letter is covered by the rental word, sitting inside it

parts.note: a let is a rental

explanation.surface: A spa town property in Bath taken on a long tenancy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bath' suggests the spa city; it is the Marquess of Bath, whose Wiltshire stately home is Longleat.
explanation.definitionFit: Longleat House is the seat of the Marquess of Bath, so it is that peer's home site.

clue.text: 5 down's bag is large, with small point

parts.note: and means with
a cape is a headland or point

explanation.surface: A description of a celebrated man's large bag, with a small point to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bag' means a person's speciality or thing, not a sack.
explanation.definitionFit: Capability Brown's field was designing landscapes for country estates, so that was his speciality.

clue.text: Palace establishment ordered to release various stats

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order
the letters of a second word are let go from the shuffled pool

explanation.surface: The establishment has been told to publish assorted statistics.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle ESTABLISHMENT and take away the letters of STATS ('various' marks them as in any order).
explanation.definitionFit: Blenheim Palace in Oxfordshire is a famous stately home, birthplace of Churchill and a Capability Brown landscape.

clue.text: Knight left at once, galloping across line

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit across the line letter, holding it inside
galloping suggests wild motion, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A knight rode off immediately, galloping across a line.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of AT ONCE gives ANCEOT, which takes the L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Lancelot is the most famous knight of King Arthur's Round Table.

clue.text: Recall crew tackling crown of elm tree

indicators.note: tackling means taking hold of, so the turned word holds the letter
to recall is to call back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a crew is the men

indicators.note: a crown is the top, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Workers are called back to deal with the top of an elm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recall' turns MEN into NEM, which takes in the E.
explanation.definitionFit: The neem is an Indian tree of the mahogany family, valued for its oil.

clue.text: Trees in not very attractive Hampshire town

indicators.note: 'not' means without, so those letters are removed

parts.note: Aldershot is a garrison town in Hampshire, a county in southern England
hot is slang for very attractive

explanation.surface: Trees growing in a rather plain town in Hampshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Alders are trees of the birch family that grow in damp ground.

clue.text: Directors begin dithering in spring's union rounds

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go inside the springs

parts.note: a spring is a well, and the 's makes it plural
D is an abbreviation for director, so directors are DD

indicators.note: dithering is wavering this way and that, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Directors start to waver over a union during spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' is a marriage, not a trade union; 'dithering' makes EDDINGB.
explanation.definitionFit: Church bells are rung in peals, or rounds, to celebrate a marriage, so union rounds are these bells.

clue.text: Classic order: cook most of cereal

parts.note: to do food is to cook it

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its last letter

parts.note: rice is a cereal

explanation.surface: A breakfast instruction: prepare nearly all the cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' is an architectural term, not a command.
explanation.definitionFit: The Doric is one of the classical orders of Greek architecture, with plain capitals.

clue.text: Buff fine beard

parts.note: F is the pencil abbreviation for fine
an awn is the bristly beard on an ear of barley or other grass

explanation.surface: A description of a pale, fine-looking beard.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are names of a light yellowish-brown colour.

clue.text: He enjoyed 9, lodge or genteel houses

indicators.note: the phrase houses the letters, holding them within its words

explanation.surface: A gentleman who was fond of lodges or genteel houses.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' refers to the answer at 9 across, a position of royal authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Six British monarchs have borne this name, so a holder of it enjoyed the throne.

clue.text: Topper, old and jaunty, covers topless 13

indicators.note: the jaunty word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: pert means jaunty or lively

indicators.note: losing its top removes the first letter

parts.note: refers to the answer at 13 across, a sunken ditch

explanation.surface: An old, jaunty figure covers up someone who has gone topless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topper' is slang for a tall silk hat, not a person who outdoes others; 'topless' leaves AHA.
explanation.definitionFit: A topper is a top hat, and an opera hat is a collapsible top hat.

clue.text: He tends neat laurel screening mock bananas

indicators.note: screening means hiding behind a cover, so the comedian's name surrounds the shuffled letters

parts.note: Stan Laurel was the comic partner of Oliver Hardy

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tidy gardener tends a laurel hedge that hides joke banana plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' is the old word for cattle, not tidy; 'laurel' is the comedian, not a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockman looks after livestock, and neat is an archaic word for cattle.

clue.text: Queen is reclining in shade

indicators.note: lying back means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: Anne was a Queen of England

explanation.surface: The Queen relaxes on a lounger in the shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is an earthy reddish-brown pigment, so it is a colour, or shade.
